abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    As algorithmic pricing becomes more prevalent, understanding consumer responses to AI‐set prices is increasingly important. Across two experiments with Chilean students (
                    N
                     = 165) and U.S. consumers (
                    N
                     = 631), we examined how the price‐setting agent (AI vs. human) and price format (round vs. just‐below) influence consumer responses. Study 1 provides directional evidence that consumers respond less favorably to AI‐set prices and supports a preference for round over just‐below prices when pricing is attributed to AI. Study 2 supports the less favorable response to AI pricing and provides directional evidence for the predicted price‐format effect. Importantly, Study 2 provides evidence consistent with perceived manipulation as an underlying mechanism: just‐below prices heighten perceptions that AI pricing is intended to influence or exploit consumers, reducing recommendation likelihood and purchase intention. These findings extend research on algorithmic pricing, psychological pricing, and digital nudging.

ur.tldr: 研究AI与人类定价对消费者反应的影响。两项实验（智利学生165人、美国消费者631人）发现：消费者对AI定价反应更消极；AI定价时偏好整数价格而非尾数价格；机制为尾数价格加剧了消费者对AI定价意图的操控感，进而降低推荐意愿与购买意向。
